rendered: The review does not say that. Nothing in the document calls direct recycling the most widely commercialized route. Its commercial picture is different: the pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical routes are the ones described as commercialized, recovering valuable metals and salts, while direct recycling is described as still at the lab scale.[1][2] Direct recycling is presented as promising for its low-temperature, low-energy character, but the review says many challenges keep it at the lab scale. A key barrier is the multiplicity of cathode chemistries, because single-cathode input is preferred to recover high-purity cathode powder.[3][4][5] The review also notes that direct recycling could have the lowest environmental impacts, but more research is still needed to validate this.[6]
